content:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate in region us-west-2 (zone: us-west-2c). ELB target health checks failing. Auto-remediation attempted: none.

oncall-sre: acked — paging oncall. I'm looking. :eyes:

alice: seeing sustained 502/504 from edge → origin, plus ELB target group shows ~30% unhealthy in us-west-2c. Other AZs mostly fine.

bob: logs from a few hosts in us-west-2c show EBS I/O timeouts and kernel messages: (snippet)
```
[ 1234.567890] sd 0:0:0:0: [xvda] I/O error, dev xvda, sector 98304
[ 1235.678901] EXT4-fs error (device xvda1): ext4_journal_start_sb: Detected aborted journal
```

carol: ELB health check failures correlate with the instances showing EBS errors. Looks like instances losing volumes intermittently which breaks the runtime and makes the process unresponsive to health probes.

eng-runtime: can we drain or detach those targets from the LB quickly? We should avoid automatic replace if EBS detach might cause stuck ENIs.

oncall-sre: doing tactical: marking targets unhealthy in TG and removing them from rotation. Running drain on targets with large in-flight KV cache to avoid state loss.

prod-support: customer-impact: several hosted API customers reporting timeouts and increased latencies for generation calls, roughly 12% of requests in us-west-2 saw errors in last 10m. CS is collecting customer list for comms.

networking-aws-liaison: opening AWS ticket now (case 1234567890). Noting EBS control plane errors in us-west-2c reported by AWS health.

alice: mitigation steps I'm running now:
```bash
# mark targets out of service
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn $TG_ARN --targets Id=i-0abcde12345 --region us-west-2
# reduce LB health-check grace so traffic fails fast for bad instances
aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn $TG_ARN --health-check-interval-seconds 10 --region us-west-2
```

bob: also scaling up capacity in us-west-2a/b and spinning up spare fleet in eu-west-1 as emergency failover. Starting a dedicated dedicated fleet with pinned models to keep tails low.

eng-runtime: note — KV cache warmup will take ~2-3 minutes for new nodes. We'll route small % traffic while warming. Set canary 5% route to eu-west-1 for critical customers.

incident-bot: PST: page sent to alice, bob, carol, oncall-sre.

prod-support: Customer-success: please prepare an initial status page blurb: short description, affected region us-west-2 (us-west-2c primarily), impact: elevated 5xx/latency on generation endpoints, mitigation steps, ETA unknown.

customer-success: drafting now. Will say: "We are investigating elevated errors for inference endpoints in us-west-2. We have isolated the issue to EC2 instances in a single AZ (us-west-2c) experiencing EBS I/O errors which caused ELB health check failures and request errors. Traffic is being shifted away from the affected AZ and we are coordinating with AWS Support for a resolution. We will update in 30 minutes."

carol: AWS support responded — they're seeing degraded EBS control plane in us-west-2c and are performing host-level remediation. They recommend evacuating instances from that AZ if immediate recovery is required.

oncall-sre: executing cross-AZ shift via Route53 weighted rules: lowering weights for us-west-2c endpoints to 0 and increasing us-west-2a/b. TTL set to 20s to speed propagation.

alice: applied route53 change (change-id Z3ABCDEFG123). Confirmed by curl from multiple vantage points: traffic to model endpoints from our edge is now going ~95% to a/b. Error rates starting to drop.

bob: spun up 10 warm instances in eu-west-1 with models pinned (m-quantized-v2). Adding to fallback pool for enterprise customers.

eng-runtime: reminder — when we re-register instances back to TG, we need to ensure readiness probe checks application-level /healthz and KV cache warmed to avoid immediate failures and to keep latency SLOs.

customer-success: drafting customer communication update 1: 1) What happened, 2) who's impacted, 3) mitigation in progress (traffic shifted, AWS ticket open), 4) next update in 30min.

oncall-sre: handing off to bob for next hour (need a break). bob you have page. :handoff:

bob: taking over. I'll continue monitoring AWS case and metrics. If AWS can't fix within 45m, we'll keep weighted failover and consider AZ quarantine for longer.

prod-support: CC engineering for post-incident RCA and potential plan: reduce per-AZ scaling pressure and ensure cross-AZ capacity buffer for critical customers.

eng-runtime: action item logged: increase cross-AZ reserve instances in us-west-2 from 10%->25% of baseline, automated warm-up, and add runbook step for faster Route53 weight flips.

networking-aws-liaison: AWS case updated: "Engineering is replacing problem hosts and verifying EBS control plane after repair". ETA currently 45-90 minutes but could change.

alice: metrics now show 5xx rate back down to baseline in region overall (us-west-2) after shift. us-west-2c still flaky.

customer-success: posting update to status page now with current mitigation and link to support ticket for customers who want to open dedicated cases.

bob: monitoring logs and will start controlled reintroduce of healthy instances from us-west-2c when AWS confirms EBS stability. Do not auto-scale into that AZ until confirmed.

incident-bot: NOTE: please file a postmortem and link runbook items. Incident severity set to Sev2.

carol: recording timeline for postmortem: detection -> 2174507777, mitigation (traffic shift + deregister) -> 2174508400, AWS contacted -> 2174508800, handoff to bob -> 2174509300, stabilization observed -> 2174511200.

prod-support: customer list attached in private channel for comms followups.

bob: closing the active mitigation note: keep Route53 weights at current config until AWS confirms, ready to reintroduce with warm-up probes. I'll update here with any AWS status changes.

customer-success: thanks — we'll prepare an external post-incident update after RCA.

alice: small ops note for RCA: collect kernel logs, EBS metrics, ELB target health events, Route53 change history, and scaling events. Also check whether any scheduled maintenance overlapped.

bob: copying AWS case number and contact to ticketing system. Will escalate to TAM if not fixed in 1 hour.

incident-bot: Incident thread closed for immediate action; remain subscribed for updates.
